title: Erasures, not errors: machine-checked arithmetic and the correction record of the Linear A accounting tablets (research report and toolkit)
description:
Machine-checked arithmetic, hypothesis testing, and apparatus mining over the Linear A corpus (GORILA / J. Younger, via lineara.xyz). Key findings: (1) column-aware summation checks (28 checks, 10 exact) cross-referenced with the critical apparatus of GORILA I show that all genuinely deviating tablets carry erasures/corrections in their numeral lines, while exactly-summing tablets carry none (Fisher's exact test, p = 0.003) — the 'calculation errors' of Linear A are residues of document updates, not scribal incompetence; (2) HT 13's discrepancy is value-independent (2J = J); (3) minimal-assumption column constraints on HT 123 (H = entry-sign + 1/4, hence H ≥ 1/4) bipartition the literature on the disputed fraction values; (4) six pre-registered, git-timestamped falsifiable predictions, including for the unpublished Knossos ivory sceptre KN Zg 57–58. Includes a full draft manuscript, all analysis scripts (plain Python), the audited corpus extract, and documented data-quality corrections contributed upstream.

Analyses were performed with AI assistance (Anthropic's Claude Fable 5), directed and reviewed by the author; all critical readings were verified against the GORILA I facsimiles.
